messages:
maya: Quick sync — can someone pick up a small smoke sweep comparing A100 / H100 / L40S for our longctx 32k model (gpt-xxl-like). Not the full multi-seed sweep, just 4 configs to sanity-check p99 and steady-state throughput. I want numbers we can cite in the perf notes tomorrow.
jonathan: I can run it this afternoon. Which quant/precision profile? q4_k_m or q8? Also do we want dynamic batching on/off?
maya: thanks! Start with q4_k_m (closest to what prod uses). Run two batch sizes: 1 and 8, and both warm cache and cold-cache (cold = restart model + single request). Keep context length at 32k. Turn off dynamic merging (so consistent microbatching).
lee: pinging infra: which image + driver should jonathan use? we had the kernel patch on h100 last week.
perf-bot: scheduled run by jonathan on h100-pool-03 at 2026-03-17T16:20:00Z (run id: r-1971234). Config: model=gpt-xxl-32k, precision=q4_k_m, batch_sizes=[1,8], caches=[warm,cold], traces=perf+nvprof.
jonathan: using image redwood/runtime:prod-2026-03-10 + nvidia-driver 535.86. I will also run identical job on a100-pool-02 and l40s-pool-01.
ash: (reacts) :thumbsup:
ashley: quick note — for p99 we need at least 200 requests per config to be meaningful. If time is tight, do 100 but flag wide CI variance.
jonathan: ack. I'll do 200 per config where possible, otherwise fall back to 100 and mark in notes.
kai: small ask — capture the per-token GPU utilization and the nvlink bw for h100/a100. NVLINK differences can explain microburst p99s.
jonathan: will add nvlink and PCIe counters. Also saving per-step lat hist to /tmp/bench-1971234/*.json
maya: can you also post the small PR with the job specs so reviewers can see config? no heavy review, just visibility. link it here once created.
jonathan: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 — contains k8s job yaml and perf analysis notebook.
lee: quick code-review: lgtm for the job yaml. Suggest adding env var PERF_TAG=mini-sku-smoke for tracking in observability.
jonathan: added PERF_TAG and retriggering. Perf runs in progress: h100 done (first pass), a100 started, l40s queued.
perf-bot: run r-1971234-h100 completed: p50=22ms(batch=1), p99=154ms(batch=1), throughput=41 tok/s(batch=8). Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/r-1971234/h100/
jonathan: quick summary from h100: low variance on warm cache; cold-cache p99 spikes as expected. saving full traces.
perf-bot: run r-1971234-a100 completed: p50=25ms(batch=1), p99=170ms(batch=1), throughput=38 tok/s(batch=8). Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/r-1971234/a100/
jonathan: a100 looks ~10-12% worse on p99 vs h100 for this workload. NVLINK counters show more backpressure on a100 during longctx flush.
perf-bot: run r-1971234-l40s completed: p50=28ms(batch=1), p99=210ms(batch=1), throughput=35 tok/s(batch=8). Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/r-1971234/l40s/
ashley: thanks — these numbers are great. Can you drop the raw per-step hist and the kernel timeline into the notebook so we can slice by step?
jonathan: uploaded hist + timeline to the PR artifacts and added a short writeup in the notebook comparing kernel stalls.
kai: initial interpretation: H100 wins tail and throughput; A100 slightly worse on tail due to nvlink stalls; L40S is cheaper but higher p99 — might be viable for non-latency-sensitive batch workloads.
maya: perfect — can we capture cost-per-token rough calc for each pool (estimate using hourly price tags in infra sheet) and add to the notebook? I want a slide for tomorrow's sync.
jonathan: will add cost calc by EOD. If anyone wants more configs (quant or batch) say now, otherwise I'll finalize notes.
lee: also add a one-liner in the PR description: "smoke sweep: 3 SKUs, q4_k_m, ctx=32k, batches 1/8, warm/cold, 200 reqs" so it's discoverable.
maya: thanks team. If no objections I'll mark this done and we can use the H100 numbers for the perf page.
nash: no objections.
jonathan: done — PR updated and merged to perf-notes branch. artifacts link in PR.
maya: awesome — will include summary in tomorrow's runtime all-hands. :tada:
